title: High-molecular weight DNA extraction and small fragment removal of Ascochyta lentis
author: Johannes Wolfram JWD Debler
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgw5jxg6
materials: Freshly prepare lysis and precipitation buffers. Lysis buffer 5 mL per 500 mg of sample. EDTA is a metal ion chelator. By binding to Mg 2+ , DNase activity is stopped as it is dependent on Mg2+. Precipitation buffer 10 mL per 500 mg of sample. The DNA extraction process appeared unaffected when the lysis and precipitation buffers were not adjusted to pH 8. Note Tris-HCl and EDTA stock solutions are already at pH 8. 9% PEG8000 small fragment elimination buffer ~300 uL per 500 mg of sample.
Vortex lysis and precipitation buffers, then place both in the 55°C water bath to dissolve CTAB. Further vortexing or inverting may be needed to dissolve all CTAB. Leave buffers at 55°C until needed.

Quantify the DNA on a Nanodrop and a Qubit fluorometer (dsDNA broad-range assay) (both instruments from Thermo Fisher Scientific). The DNA is still crude and will likely have RNA and other contaminants present. For Nanodrop, use 1 μL. However, Qubit fluorometer accuracy is highly dependent on the accuracy of the amount pipetted. Use 2 μL when sample is plentiful. Using 1 μL is prone to pipetting errors.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

Quantify the DNA on a Nanodrop and a Qubit fluorometer (dsDNA broad-range assay) (both instruments from Thermo Fisher Scientific). The DNA should be pure, free of contaminants. For Nanodrop, use 1 μL. Qubit fluorometer is highly dependent on the accuracy of the amount pipetted. Use 2 μL when sample is plentiful. Using 1 μL is prone to pipetting errors. For pure DNA, Nanodrop: Qubit quantifications are 1:1. Expect 10-30% recovery relative to total input.

steps.title: Harvest and wash mycelium
steps.instruction: Prepare ~500 mg of Ascochyta lentis mycelium grown in liquid YEG (0.5 % yeast extract, 5 % glucose), filter through a sterile milk‑filter disk, wash the mycelium on the filter with Milli‑Q water, and keep frozen in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Prepare 55 °C water bath
steps.instruction: Set a water bath to 55 °C; it will be used to dissolve 2 % CTAB solutions and to precipitate DNA with CTAB.

steps.title: Chill mortar and pestle
steps.instruction: Place a sterile mortar and pestle inside an insulated container (e.g., an ice‑box lid) and pour liquid nitrogen into the container to keep the tools chilled.

steps.title: Grind frozen mycelium
steps.instruction: Add the frozen mycelium to the chilled mortar and grind for 1–2 min, keeping the mortar and pestle surrounded by liquid nitrogen to maintain low temperature.

steps.title: Transfer to lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer the ground mycelium to 5 mL of lysis buffer in a 15 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Add RNase A and Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add RNase A and Proteinase K to the lysate at 50–100 µg mL⁻¹ each (both can coexist in the same solution).

steps.title: Mix and incubate lysate
steps.instruction: Vortex and invert the tube to mix, then incubate at 55 °C for at least 1 h.

steps.title: Add chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1, v/v) and mix by inverting 10–15 times to temporarily emulsify the phases.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 5 000 rcf for 10 min at 20 °C, then transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new 15 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Repeat chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Perform a second extraction by adding an equal volume of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol, mixing, centrifuging (5 000 rcf, 10 min, 20 °C) and transferring the aqueous phase.

steps.title: Add precipitation buffer
steps.instruction: Add two volumes of precipitation buffer to the aqueous phase, mix by inverting, and incubate at 55 °C for 1 h or until white CTAB‑DNA crystals are observed.

steps.title: Pellet CTAB‑DNA complex
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 5 000 rcf for 30 min at 20 °C to pellet the CTAB‑DNA crystals.

steps.title: Decant supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully decant the supernatant without disturbing the fragile pellet.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Add freshly prepared 70 % ethanol (~5 mL) to cover the pellet, let soak for 15 min at room temperature to remove salts and residual CTAB.

steps.title: Centrifuge and decant ethanol
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 5 000 rcf for 10 min, then carefully decant the ethanol supernatant.

steps.title: Air‑dry pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet for 10–15 min (or until all ethanol has evaporated).

steps.title: Dissolve DNA in TE
steps.instruction: Gently dissolve the pellet in ≤300 µL of 0.1× TE (nuclease‑free water) by flicking the tube; avoid vigorous pipetting to prevent shearing. Volume can be 250 µL if desired.

steps.title: Transfer to LoBind tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the dissolved DNA to a 1.5 mL DNA LoBind Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Store DNA at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Store the DNA at 4 °C to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles; DNA integrity remains stable for extended periods at this temperature.

steps.title: PEG precipitation of small fragments
steps.instruction: Combine 250 µL DNA with 250 µL 9 % PEG buffer, mix gently, and incubate for 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Centrifuge PEG pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture for 30 min at 10 000 rcf at room temperature to pellet high‑molecular‑weight DNA.

steps.title: Wash PEG pellet with ethanol
steps.instruction: Cover the pellet with 300–500 µL 80 % ethanol, incubate 5 min at room temperature, then spin 5 min at 10 000 rcf (room temperature). Repeat this wash once more.
